summary: Historical volatility: the standard deviation of 10-bar log returns, scaled to a yearly figure with 252 periods by default.
overview: Historical Volatility shows how much price has been moving, as a percentage, in its own pane. Higher readings mean bigger day-to-day changes.
By default it is annualized so values can be read as a yearly figure.
how: Log return = ln(close / previous close). HV = standard deviation of log returns over 10 bars x square root of periods per year x 100.
Use 252 for daily bars, 52 for weekly and 12 for monthly. Turn off Annualize to see per-bar volatility.
use: Use it to compare how volatile a symbol is now versus before.
Some traders compare historical volatility with expected volatility from options.
Watch for very low readings, which can come before larger moves.
Use it to adjust position size.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
On intraday charts set Periods Per Year to match the bar count, or turn off annualizing.
